_verificationNote: AUDITED 2026-08-15 — 18 of 20 figures CONFIRMED CORRECT; two corrections identified and one lever missing. Applies to: TAX YEAR 2026. The sibling 'verificationNote' key predates this audit and is now stale. CONFIRMED against IRS Notice 2025-67 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/n-25-67.pdf, fetched 2026-08-15): elective401kCents $24,500 (§402(g)(1); §457(e)(15) is also $24,500 so the shared field is safe), catchUp401k50Cents $8,000 (§414(v)(2)(B)(i)), iraCents $7,500 (§219(b)(5)(A)), iraCatchUp50Cents $1,100 (§219(b)(5)(B)(ii)), sepOverallCapCents $72,000 (§415(c)(1)(A)), and IRA phase-outs for coveredJoint $129k–$149k, spouseCoveredJoint $242k–$252k, marriedSeparate $0–$10k (the last is statutorily NOT indexed and must never be changed). CONFIRMED against Rev. Proc. 2025-19 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-19.pdf): hsaSelfOnlyCents $4,400, hsaFamilyCents $8,750. CONFIRMED against 26 U.S.C. §223(b)(3)(B) on govinfo: hsaCatchUp55Cents $1,000, statutory and not indexed. CONFIRMED against SSA's Federal Register notice FR Doc. 2025-19763 (3 Nov 2025), fetched via https://api.govinfo.gov/packages/FR-2025-11-03/granules/2025-19763/htm : ssWageBaseCents $184,500. CONFIRMED against govinfo US Code: sepEmployerPctBps 25% (§404(h)(1)(C)), seTaxSsRateBps 12.4% (§1401(a)), seTaxMedicareRateBps 2.9% (§1401(b)(1)), seTaxRateBps 15.3% (their sum), seNetEarningsFactorBps 92.35% (§1402(a)(12), = 100% minus half of 15.3%, expressly excluding the 0.9% additional Medicare tax). CORRECTED 2026-08-15 — iraPhaseOut.coveredSingleFromCents/ToCents held 7900000/8900000 ($79k–$89k), which are the 2025 values; Notice 2025-67 states 'the deduction ... is phased out for single individuals and heads of household who are active participants ... between $81,000 and $91,000, increased from between $79,000 and $89,000', so they are now 8100000/9100000. The old values wrongly told a single filer with MAGI between $89k and $91k that the traditional-IRA deduction was fully phased out, hiding a live MAGI-reduction lever from exactly the income band that sits near the cliff for a one-person household. MISSING — the SECURE 2.0 age 60-63 'super catch-up' under §414(v)(2)(E)(i) is $11,250 for 2026 (confirmed in Notice 2025-67; it applies INSTEAD OF, not in addition to, the $8,000 age-50 catch-up). It is real, in force, and not modeled here — $3,250 of extra MAGI reduction unavailable to 60-63-year-olds, who are the likeliest pre-Medicare marketplace enrollees near the cliff. ALSO NOT MODELED, from Rev. Proc. 2025-19 §2.01(2): the 2026 HDHP definition (minimum deductible $1,700 self-only / $3,400 family; out-of-pocket maximum $8,500 / $17,000) is a genuine eligibility gate on the HSA lever. Values left unchanged in this pass per audit scope. WHERE TO RE-CHECK ANNUALLY: HSA amounts ~May, retirement/IRA COLAs ~October, both at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/ ; SSA wage base ~late October via the govinfo search API (ssa.gov returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients). See VERIFICATION-STATUS.md.
